documents.t: A ship is the primary way to travel through space, fight enemies, and carry cargo. Every ship is built around a Ship Core block — the single block that defines the ship.
Action Key Enter a ship (look at core) R Exit a ship (look away from ship) R When you enter a ship you are placed directly into its Ship Core. From there you can switch between the two ship modes.
Press Z to toggle between flight mode and build mode while inside a ship.

Every ship has three resource bars visible in the HUD: Bar Colour Description Hull / HP Red Total hull health. Reaches zero → ship destroyed Shield Blue Absorbs incoming damage before hull is hit Power Green Energy available for weapons, thrusters, and shields

Action Key Accelerate forward W Decelerate / reverse S Strafe up Space Strafe down Left Ctrl Strafe left / right A / D Roll left / right Q / E Fire active weapon Left Mouse Button Cycle weapon slots 1–9, 0 / Mouse wheel Select target F Open weapon panel G Open structure panel Delete

If your reactor becomes damaged to the point of Overheating, or something else goes wrong with your systems state, you can Reboot your ship. During Reboot, a ship's systems are nonfunctional, but they are reset to a fresh state after the reboot is complete.
StarMade uses a block-group system to determine how sets of same-type blocks behave together. This is most important for weapons, where grouping affects how shots are fired.

A block group is a set of blocks of the same type that are all touching each other (face-to-face, not diagonal). A solid cube is one block group. A straight line is also one block group. A single isolated block is its own group.

Reactors are the core of your ship, generating the energy that all other ship systems use to function, and are the central linking point for your reactor chambers, which modify other ship systems. See Reactors.

Chambers are sub-systems that branch off from your reactor and modify the function of other systems on your ship (such as shields, jump drives, and thrusters), or give you new systems (such as scanners and stealth drives). See Chambers.
Thruster modules add to your ship's maximum speed and acceleration. More blocks equals more thrust. Higher thrust to mass ratio gives you a higher top speed. See Thrusters.
Shield modules generate a shield that absorbs damage before it reaches your hull. Shield recharge requires power, so size your reactors to support your shield blocks. See Shields.

Each contiguous group of weapon, salvager, or astrotech barrel/module blocks fires as a single shot. You can choose between: Layout Effect All barrels in one touching group One powerful shot Multiple separate groups Multiple weaker simultaneous shots The weapon or salvage computer is a separate block and doesn't need to touch the barrels — it is connected via the link system. See Weapons and Salvagers.

Thrusters are modules that allow you to move your ship, and consume energy from your Reactor in order to do so. Thrusters have a linear power consumption per module, but diminishing returns on how much thrust each thruster module on a ship produces. Larger ships will require more thrusters and more power to move at the same speed as a smaller ship.

A ship's thrust to mass ratio (TMR) determines its maximum speed, as well as how fast it can accelerate. The maximum TMR that grants increased top speed is 5.0, and this is the highest possible TWR that will be indicated directly in the Advanced Build interface. (You can, however, continue adding thrusters for pure maneuverability until the game's sanity limit of 10:1 thrust to mass. Thrust capacity beyond that serves no purpose whatsoever.)

Opening the radial menu to Ship -> Thrusters opens the Thruster Management menu. In this menu, you can assign the percentage of thrust that goes to each axis of travel, as well as rotational thrust and thrust routed to Repulsors instead of primary movement. You can also enable "Inherit Thrusters From Docks" to add thrust from docked ships to the main ship, and enable or disable automatic dampeners (passive braking that prevents the ship from drifting forever without control input).
Repulsors use thrust to allow a ship to automatically hover off the ground inside of a gravity field.
Chambers can increase your ship's max speed or unlock a "Thrust Blast" system for sudden bursts of acceleration. See the Chambers guide for more details.

StarMade has three primary weapon types, three utility weapons, and explosive warhead blocks. Primary weapons can be linked to a secondary weapon to alter the functions and stats of the primary weapon, and can be linked to an effect system to alter its damage type distribution.

Primary Weapons: Weapon Primary Role Secondary Role Cannon Simple direct-fire projectile Shorter range, higher rate of fire Missile Complex explosive projectile Higher damage, charge up time Damage Beam Hitscan damage beam Longer range, slower rate of fire Utility Weapons (no direct damage): Weapon Role Push Pulse Knocks back nearby ships; deals no direct damage Tractor Beam Pulls, pushes, or tows ships and loose objects Astrotech Beam Repairs damaged or destroyed blocks on ships Block Weapons (deal damage on block contact): Weapon Role Warhead Explodes on contact with another ship; ignores shields

Every weapon system consists of two block types: Weapon Computer — the controller. Assign it to a hotbar slot. One per weapon system. Weapon Modules — the actual firepower. More modules = more damage, albeit with diminishing returns on larger and larger weapons.

Place a Weapon Computer on your ship in build mode. Place Weapon Modules anywhere on the ship (they don't need to touch the computer). Open the Weapon Panel (G). Drag the computer into a hotbar slot. Close the panel, switch to flight mode, and select the weapon slot. Weapon Computer Module Cannon Cannon Computer Cannon Barrel Missile Missile Computer Missile Tube Beam Damage Beam Computer Damage Beam Module Push Pulse Push Pulse Computer Push Pulse Module Tractor Beam Tractor Beam Computer Tractor Beam Module

By linking a Secondary Weapon computer and modules to a Primary Weapon, you can alter the function of the primary weapon, like its range, reload speed, and damage. Including the 3 basic primary weapons, there are 12 total Weapon Combinations, each with unique stats and function. The ratio of weapon modules linked to the Secondary Weapon compared to the Primary Weapon determines how much of the modification effect is applied, with 100% of the effect being applied at a 1:1 ratio. Experiment with partial secondary effects to find the perfect weapon for your niche! A weapon computer can only be used in one combination at a time. Primary Weapon Cannon Secondary Damage Beam Secondary Missile Secondary No Secondary Cannon Machine Gun Sniper Cannon Charge Cannon Basic Cannon Damage Beam Constant Beam Sniper Beam Charge Beam Burst Beam Missile Heat-Seeking Swarms Long Range Lock On Inertia Bomb Dumbfire Missile Missile/Missile creates a special shield-ignoring bomb that has no velocity of its own and must be launched from a fast moving ship.

Connecting certain effect systems to a weapon computer changes the damage type distribution (Kinetic, Heat, EM). This will make a weapon stronger against one type of defenses and weaker against the others. At a 1:1 Primary Weapon to Effect System ratio, the damage will be increased by 33.3% for the specified damage type and reduced by 16.6% for the other two types. A primary weapon can be linked to both a secondary weapon and an effect system at the same time. Each weapon type has a different default damage distribution, making them better suited for dealing with different types of targets. Weapon Type Kinetic Heat EM Cannons 50% 16.6% 33.3% Damage Beams 16.6% 33.3% 50% Missiles 16.6% 50% 33.3% See the Armor & Damage guide for how damage types interact with shields and armor.

Open the Weapon Panel (G). Find your primary weapon computer in the list. Drag the secondary weapon computer into the secondary slot of the primary. The coloured borders on the computers in the world indicate the connection. To unlink, drag the secondary out of its slot and drop it in the unlink box. You can also link and unlink in-world: press C on the primary computer, then V on the secondary computer.

Every weapon barrel produces some heat when it fires, and cannot fire if the ship has no heat capacity remaining. Consequently, a ship with too many separate weapon barrels may not be able to fire them continuously. Placing Heat Sinks increases your ship's Heat Capacity at the cost of consuming some power. However, adding more Heat Sinks has diminishing returns, with the first few hundred blocks giving a great deal of extra Heat Capacity and further ones adding incrementally less.

Missiles require Missile Capacity to fire. Missile Capacity Modules give a ship Missile Capacity, which is consumed when firing a missile. If a ship's Missile Capacity is not full, it will start reloading, with the length of time depending on how much Missile Capacity the ship has. Like Heat Sinks and weapons themselves, each Missile Capacity Module added gives diminishing returns, with the first few blocks giving a lot of Missile Capacity, but further capacity requiring exponentially more modules for each additional unit. This creates a soft cap on the number of missiles that a single ship can actually fire in a single volley.
Link a Light Source block to a weapon computer (using C to select, then V to connect) to change the colour of that weapon's projectiles to match the light colour.
Utility weapons do no damage on their own, instead having some sort of support function to either reduce the effectiveness of an enemy or boost the effectiveness of your own ships.
Push Pulse projects an area of effect pulse that pushes ships away from its origin point. The more modules, the larger and more powerful the pushing effect is.

Tractor Beams can push, pull, and stop a ship or asteroid by applying force at the point of the beam's impact. More modules increases the tractor strength. A small, slowly drifting asteroid is much easier to stop than a large ship that is actively fighting the tractor beam with its own thrusters.

Astrotech beams can repair damaged blocks and restore destroyed blocks on a ship. The ship must not have been edited with build mode after the blocks were destroyed for it to be repaired by an astrotech beam, as astrotech restores the ship to its last saved state. More modules increases the amount of blocks restored with each burst of the beam. There is a cooldown period after taking block damage before any blocks can be repaired by an astrotech beam.

Warheads are explosive blocks that detonate when hit by a weapon or when they collide with another object. All warheads in a contiguous group are automatically linked together and will detonate together, with the strength of the explosion determined by how many blocks are in the group. The explosion from warheads ignores shields. Warheads can be combined with shootout rails and a Bobby AI module to create powerful, single use "torpedo" ships that attempt to ram enemy ships with their warheads.

StarMade Galaxy is a new version of StarMade built in Unity SRP that one of the developers of the original game is working on in their free time. This version of the game is publicly unavailable as of the time of writing, however you can support Schema via Patreon to gain access to the experimental branch of StarMade Galaxy, but there is currently no build yet. Note that this is completely optional, and that the official Java version is still maintained and widely used throughout the community. If you're new to StarMade the suggestion remains to stick to the Java version from Steam or the official StarMade site. There is a teaser trailer of StarMade Galaxy available on YouTube.

As you might expect the community has a lot of questions regarding how the two StarMades compare and what might one day be transferable. I've tried to compile the most commonly asked questions below and the answers from the developers. Please note, all of this is subject to change without notice and is just what we know so far as a community, not an actual plan for development. Asteroids are massive boulders found in space orbiting stars. They are a standard source of valuable Ores and Crystals needed for building, as well as bulk stone materials. They are harvested with ship-based Salvage Systems. Each star system's asteroids has a different rock composition, but any color of asteroid can contain the same resources.
Asteroids can occur throughout star-systems, but are primarily concentrated within Asteroid Belts. These are marked in yellow on your Map.

The primary utility of Asteroids is typically as a mining resource. Asteroids contain various types of embedded Ores, dependent upon what resources are overall common in a Star System. Asteroids may bear metallic or crystalline Ore types, but do NOT contain Gases, which must instead be harvested by other means. Asteroids can be claimed, built on, and used as a base, similar to a Space Station. However, it is impossible to save blueprints of an Asteroid, and you cannot set an Asteroid as a Home Base or use it to lay claim to a Star System. If collision damage is turned on, you may consider throwing asteroids at your enemies using Tractor Beams!
The StarMade universe is vast. Understanding its structure and using the navigation tools efficiently will save you a lot of time.
The universe is organised into sectors grouped into systems.

A sector is the basic unit of space. Your current sector coordinates ([X, Y, Z]) are always displayed at the top of your HUD next to your player name. Each sector can contain: Planets and their surrounding space Asteroid fields Trading stations and NPC structures Other players' ships and bases Empty space

A system is a 16 × 16 × 16 cube of sectors. Stars and wormholes are always located near the centre of their respective System. Resources and encounter types vary depending on how far a sector is from the star. Distance from the star affects asteroid types. Rare mineral asteroids are more likely to appear in sectors farther from the star.
Press N to open the Navigation Panel. It lists every object in your current and adjacent sectors.
Use the filter checkboxes to show or hide: Planets Asteroids Stations Ships (player and NPC) Radar beacons
Click any entry in the navigation list to select it. A selection indicator appears on your HUD pointing toward the selected object, making it easy to fly to it without having to spot it visually.

Astro Scanners are a ship system that provides information about a Star System. Similar to a weapon or utility beam, it consists of two block types: an Astro Scanner Computer that controls the system, and Astro Scanner Antenna blocks linked to the computer. Once an Astro Scanner is placed and added to your ship's hotbar, it can be used to scan whichever Star System your ship is currently in. It will reveal the locations of all planets and stations in that system on the Map screen, and also provide a report containing the names, locations, and factions of active ships found within its detection range. This report is viewable via the second tab of your Navigation Panel. Depending on which Reactor Chambers are installed on your ship, scanner reports also provide other information, such as what useful resources are available in the system.

To navigate to a specific sector coordinate: Open the Navigation Panel (N). Click the Waypoint button. Enter the [X, Y, Z] coordinates of your destination sector. A white blinking arrow appears on your HUD pointing toward the waypoint. Waypoints persist until you remove them. You can use them to mark resource-rich sectors, player bases, or planned routes.

Your starting sector usually contains a Trading Guild station — check the navigation panel immediately to locate it. Asteroid field sectors are clearly visible in space; approach any dark-coloured irregular objects. When travelling long distances, set a waypoint and use full thrust (W held). Ships have a natural speed cap per sector, but there is no global travel limit. You can select an entity in the world directly by looking at it and pressing F — this selects it in the HUD without opening the nav panel.
Raw resources are the foundation of everything you build. There are four families of raw materials, each found in different places across the universe.

Type Appearance Found On Ores Coloured rock chunks Asteroids, planet surfaces Crystal Shards Glittering crystals Asteroids, planet surfaces Gases Colourful wisps Gas Giant atmospheres, Nebulae Exotic Materials Various Various Each resource type has a different colour and name (e.g. Threns Ore, Varat Shards). For basic crafting, the specific type matters less than whether it is an ore or a shard — you just need enough of both to start.
Asteroid fields appear as clusters of irregular objects in space. Asteroids contain pockets of Ores and Crystal Shards on their surfaces and throughout their interiors, identifiable by colour.

Nebulae are massive coloured clouds of plasma, covering several star systems. Depending on the nebula type, ships within nebulae may experience various adverse effects, but will not be directly damaged. Gaseous resources can be harvested from Nebulae using a Gas Harvester. Space Stations within Nebulae can also accumulate resources passively from them using an Ambient Gas Extractor.

Gas Planets, a.k.a. Gas Giants, are massive planets with turbulent atmospheres and no reachable solid surface. Gaseous and sometimes exotic resources can be harvested from the proximity of Gas Giants using a Gas Harvester. Hot Gas Giants are superheated to such an extreme degree that their atmospheres contain vaporized forms of solid resources, which can also be harvested the same way. Space Stations in/adjacent to Gas Planet sectors can also accumulate resources passively from some Gas Giants using an Ambient Gas Extractor.

Planet surfaces contain Ore and Shard deposits far more concentrated than those in Asteroids, but they cannot be mined by ships' salvage systems. Astronauts exploring a planet's surface may even strike lucky veins, containing even more of a resource than usual. Bases built on Terrestrial Planets can also accumulate solid resources passively from some planets using a Deep Core Extractor.

A ship that is Overheating, or any unclaimed Space Station, can be harvested for blocks via the Salvage Beam. Any blocks obtained from wrecks can be used as-is or broken down into valuable Components via the Block Recycler factory. Ancient, abandoned, & decayed stations can be occasionally found floating throughout the cosmos, however upon salvage their blocks only yield Scrap Metal and Scrap Composite that must be restored to a usable state via the Micro Reprocessor.

Hold the right mouse button while looking at a resource block. Your character fires a mining beam. The block breaks after a short duration and drops items into your inventory automatically. Make sure no weapon is selected (scroll past the last weapon slot or press the mouse wheel to deselect).

To harvest solids & blocks, build a Salvage Computer and Salvage Beam Modules on your ship (same setup as weapons). Aim the salvage beam at asteroid, abandoned station, or wrecked (Overheating) ship to harvest them rapidly. Ships can mine much faster than astronaut mode and collect materials directly into the ship's storage. To harvest gases, build a Gas Harvester Computer and Gas Harvester Modules on your ship, likewise. Activating this module will begin a cycle. As long as the system is supplied with power for the entire cycle and there are resource traces present in the area, you will receive collected resources at the end.

Some locations throughout the galaxy have resources available to passively extract. Information about these locations can be obtained via the Long Range Scanner, with certain Recon Chamber upgrades. Once you have found a passive resource node, resources can be harvested using the appropriate extractor. Nebulae and Gas Giant planets can be harvested using the Ambient Gas Extractor on a Space Station nearby, whereas terrestrial planets require the Deep Core Extractor. Connecting Factory Enhancers to your Extractor will increase its potential resource extraction rate, however each node has a maximum amount of resources that can be extracted per cycle regardless of enhancers. Multiple passive extractors draining from one source node will split harvested resources amongst themselves proportionate to the amount of enhancers connected to them. Extraction will continue even while the structure is unloaded.

Resources in their raw form cannot be used directly — they must be processed into capsules/Mesh/Composite first, then into manufacturing Components. Those Components can then be used to create blocks, ships, & stations. See Crafting Basics for the full processing chain. Both Metal Mesh and Crystal Circuit are the base ingredients for nearly every craftable block in the game.
